facts.statement: The genus Copepteryx was first described by Olson and Hasegawa in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996, the two first species endemic from Japan were described by Olson and Hasegawa.

facts.statement: The name Copepteryx comes from the Greek words for 'oar' and 'wing', referring to its oar-like wings.
facts.quote: The name is derived from the Ancient Greek prefix "Kope-", meaning "oar", and "pteryx", meaning wing.

facts.statement: Copepteryx had wings heavily specialized for underwater propulsion, differing significantly from other pelecaniformes.
facts.quote: The wings were, as in all plotopterids, heavily specialized for underwater propulsion and in general shape and usage much different from all other known pelecaniformes.

facts.statement: Copepteryx hexeris was about 1.2 meters long and was larger than all other known plotopterids.
facts.quote: With total length about 1.2 m, while it is smaller than its lesser known relative C. titan, it was larger than all other known plotopterids.

facts.statement: Copepteryx titan is the largest described plotopterid, with an estimated length of around 2 meters.
facts.quote: C. titan is the largest species of plotopterid described, with an estimated total length around 2 m, once even overestimated about 3 m

facts.statement: The holotype femur of Copepteryx titan is 22 cm long and 6 cm wide, twice the size of an emperor penguin's femur.
facts.quote: Only known from a 22 cm long and 6 cm wide left femur, much larger than that of any other known plotopterid and twice as large as that of the emperor penguin

facts.statement: It is debated whether Copepteryx titan is a distinct species or represents the larger males of Copepteryx hexeris.
facts.quote: It has recently been suggested that C. titan would in fact represent the remains of male C. hexeris, as sexual dimorphism is often important in modern genera of cormorants and darters.

facts.statement: Copepteryx was a flightless bird endemic to Japan during the Oligocene, living from 28.4 to 23 million years ago.
facts.quote: Copepteryx is an extinct genus of flightless bird of the family Plotopteridae, endemic to Japan during the Oligocene living from 28.4 to 23 mya

facts.statement: Copepteryx were diving birds that nested on land and had a carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Copepteryx fueron aves buceadoras, al igual que Waimanu, que anidaban en tierra, y cuya dieta era carnívora.

facts.statement: Copepteryx is classified within the family Plotopteridae.
Copepteryx belongs to the subfamily Tonsalinae.
